title: Millridge · A Call at Night
sceneText:
Gregor asks nothing, but while he is saddling he looks at you. Once, and then he bends to the girth.

The kitchen light was still on as you went out. Martha stood in the doorway with something in her hands and watched you mount. She said nothing either.

An hour’s ride. There is no moon, and Gregor has hung a lantern for you.

What you think about on the road is this: by tomorrow morning this ride will be all over the valley.

Nobody here goes out at night. When one household’s horse goes out after dark, the whole village knows by the next day. And towards Millridge, particularly.

The porter at Millridge is not yet in bed. He sees you and shows no surprise either.

Henk is in the study in house clothes. The fire is well up. He sees you come in, puts down what is in his hand, and stands.

{@henk}“Late.”

There is no surprise on either face.

He pours two glasses, sets one in front of you, then sits back with his hands folded across his front and waits for you to speak.

You speak.

He hears you out and nods.

{@henk}“It has not been an easy year at Maplegate,” he says. “Ludwig comes home for three days a year, and the other three hundred and sixty-two rest on whoever runs the estate. Hartmann carried it eight years. You have carried it a month.”

He takes a drink.

{@henk}“Go on. What do you need.”

variants.short_of_trust_open:
He hears you out, and one eyebrow moves.

Then he smiles. It is unlike every smile he has had so far: the usual ones are for you; this one is for himself.

He puts the glass down and leans back in the chair.
variants.short_of_trust_count_deferred: {@henk}“I have had you to dinner once, asked you to a hunt once, and put a proposal to you once about carrying timber,” he says. “That last one you have still not answered.”
variants.short_of_trust_count_accepted: {@henk}“I have had you to dinner once, asked you to a hunt once, and put a proposal to you once about carrying timber,” he says. “That last one you took up on the spot.”
variants.short_of_trust_count_refused: {@henk}“I have had you to dinner once, asked you to a hunt once, and put a proposal to you once about carrying timber,” he says. “That last one you turned down in front of people.”
variants.short_of_trust_count_absent: {@henk}“I have asked you to dinner once, and to a hunt once,” he says.
variants.short_of_trust_close:
{@henk}“I am not keeping accounts,” he says. “I am only saying that you and I are not yet on those terms.”

He stands, goes over to the desk, takes something out of a drawer and sets it in front of you.

One guldmark.

{@henk}“Take it,” he says. “Get something for the horse on the road. Do not let it go hungry.”

He does not sit down again.

{@henk}“Mind yourself riding back,” he says. “That road is poor in autumn.”

The porter sees you out.

On the way home you think of Martha standing in the kitchen doorway, watching you mount.

effects.logEntry: In the study at Millridge you said you needed a good deal.

choices.resultText:
He did not make you say it twice.

{@henk}“Right,” he says, and calls out through the door.

Somebody answers. For the next quarter of an hour the Millridge men are loading the cart. Grain, timber, a small bag of money absurdly heavy for its size. You stand in the yard and watch them load. One of them comes over to ask what weight the boards will take, and you cannot tell him, so he goes and looks himself.

Henk comes out with a coat over his shoulders and stands beside you.

{@henk}“Enough for the winter,” he says. “Keep what is over; it will do for the spring sowing as well.”

You say the amount is too much.

{@henk}“Neighbours.”

He looks towards Maplegate, not at you.

{@henk}“There will come a time when you are of use to me.”

That is all of it. He does not say when, and he does not say what, and he does not ask you to agree to anything.

But you both know.

You stand together and watch them finish loading. He claps you on the shoulder and says to mind the road.

You ride home slowly. The cart is heavy, the horse goes slowly, the lantern swings.

You agreed to nothing.

But what you are carrying home is something that, once accepted, can never again be accounted for.

effects.logEntry: At Millridge you asked for cash.

choices.resultText:
{@henk}“Money is easy.”

A cloth bag is brought for him. He does not count it; he pushes it straight across.

The amount is exactly the amount you needed. You never named a figure.

{@henk}“Call it a loan from me,” he says, smiling. “Repay it whenever.”

You put the bag in an inside pocket. It is heavier than you expected.

effects.logEntry: At Millridge you asked for grain and timber.

choices.resultText:
{@henk}“Grain and wood I have,” he says. “Wood especially.”

He does not explain why he has so much wood, and you do not pick that up.

Loading takes a while. He stands under the eaves and watches, and goes inside once in the middle of it. When he comes out there is a coat in his hand. Not for you. For the man driving.

{@henk}“Put it all on the account,” he says. “We will settle up by and by.”

effects.logEntry: You asked for nothing at Millridge and rode back to Maplegate empty.

choices.resultText:
You stand up and say you have disturbed him.

He is taken aback. For several seconds neither of you says anything.

The Baron is waiting for you to finish. You have finished.

{@henk}“Ah,” he says.

He stands as well, and the smile goes back on his face, though in your eyes it is the first time it does not fit him at all.

{@henk}“Mind the road.”

He sees you to the study door. Half the lamps in the corridor are already out.

{@henk}“About Maplegate,” he says as you are going out. “If you ever come round to it, any time.”

“I am not moving house.”

The wind on the ride home is stronger than it was coming out.

You brought nothing back, but the whole valley will know tomorrow that you went.
